angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 5,502,291 km at 29.09 pc = 2.53 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 53229: distance 29.087 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.006), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 29.087 +/- 0.175 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 32.9210 +/- 0.1775 mas (same row, RUWE 2.17), 185.5 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 7.909 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 53229: radius 7.909 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 28.492 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.053) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 5,502,291 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 4745 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 53229: effective temperature 4745 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.063) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 53229: effective temperature 4745 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.063) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, * 46 LMi: projected rotation speed 2.1 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2008AJ....135..209M)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 2.73 from 2013ApJ...764...78R; the 12 published values span log g 2.5 to 3, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.1% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2013ApJ...764...78R)
